comments.author: reeddavid
comments.story: Ask HN: What are some interesting projects to reuse your old devices?
comments.why: Explains why the Fresnel lens daylight panel works well
comments.text: Not a company, but sharing a personal project: I got a free broken 55" TV and turned it into a big daylight panel. I got a great explanation of why this works well (fresnel lens) from the DIY Perks channel on YouTube: Turning Smashed TVs into Realistic Artificial Daylight ( [VIDEO] ). The main board had failed so the screen was black and the backlight cycled on and off. After disconnecting the main board, the backlight stayed on. I am using the existing LED lights, but may replace them with the excellent color quality LEDs recommended by DIY Perks.

comments.author: jsilence
comments.story: Rooms can be as bright as the outdoors
comments.why: DIY directions for recycling LCD monitors into artificial windows
comments.text: It is possible to recycle old LCD monitors into articficial windows that have a very real feel to them. The diffraction lenses for the backlight direct the light in a way that makes it appear sun like. Of course this is only about the direction and not about the spectrum, but it might be possible to find LED strips with a high CRI. Any feedback would be appreciated. DIY directions on YT: [VIDEO]

comments.author: yterdy
comments.story: Millions of smart meters will brick it when 2G and 3G turns off
comments.why: Example of repurposing broken TVs as light panels
comments.text: I disagree. The difficulty of replacing tech changes one's relationship to one's devices. Things that I see people throw away as "e-waste" are really, "Things someone couldn't be assed to repair or repurpose." For example, broken TVs could be repurposed as large light panels ( [VIDEO] ), or their main boards could be hacked for fun and profit ( [LINK] ). When I see a broken TV, even one I don't own, that's where the pain comes from. Same with phones, laptops, etc. We throw away so mny perfectly good general-purpose computers, it's insane. When we run out of a necessary resource for their manufacture, will we just be scavenging them?
